question: During the streamer's trip to Shanghai, what flavors of ice cream did the streamer get at the Five Snowman stores and eat all along the way?

rollouts.answer: The documented Shanghai ice-cream stop shows a chocolate-and-vanilla combination, with the cone ultimately served as vanilla soft-serve. He then ate the vanilla cone while walking through the crowd (around 176,328-176,478 seconds). I found evidence for one such Shanghai shop-not five separate snowman stores.
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search(event_steps/topic_facts/episodes/visual_clips) x5 -> run_sql(episodes ice-cream LIKE) x2 -> run_sql(snowman UNION) -> semantic_search x2 -> run_sql(episodes video/1h/6h) -> run_sql(entities snow/ice) -> semantic_search(entities/topic_facts) -> run_sql(flavor/vanilla/chocolate LIKE) -> clip_qa(176250-177100) -> run_sql(ice cream global) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: run_sql UNION search for 'snowman' across episodes/event_steps/topic_facts returns no hit near 176k s and only an unrelated 352k s hit, so the store's actual name/brand is never confirmed in DB text.
clip_qa on 176250-177100 answers 'chocolate and vanilla... cone visibly vanilla soft serve', matching the DB captions; no mention of taro or purple color.

rollouts.failure_point: Flavor misidentified: DB captions and the visual sub-agent both read the cone as vanilla, not taro; agent correctly found the single Shanghai ice-cream stop and correctly noted only one shop (not five), but reported the wrong flavor pair.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Pulled logical-time frames 176328-176460 (source video 14, offset ~19050-19182) directly; the cone at 176440-176450 is cream/off-white with a brown drizzle on top, consistent with what the DB/clip_qa called 'chocolate-vanilla', not an obviously purple taro color under the shop's warm/green lighting.

rollouts.answer: He got a chocolate-and-vanilla twist-alternating chocolate and vanilla soft-serve-and ate it along the way. The shop footage shows him ordering the chocolate-vanilla combo and then eating the swirled cone.

rollouts.answer: Lists 5 different flavors across the whole video (chocolate-vanilla ~176k, corn ~192k, chili ~207k, vanilla-strawberry ~240k, vanilla ~264k), interpreting 'five snowman stores' as five separate arbitrary ice-cream stops.

decisive_steps.what_happened: Agent generalized 'five' in the question to mean five distinct ice-cream-eating moments across the entire video timeline rather than a single named store chain visited near 176k s, and ran clip_qa on each candidate moment it found via broad searches.

rollouts.failure_point: Question misinterpretation: took 'Five Snowman' (a store/brand name) as a literal count of separate stores/flavors to enumerate, diluting the one partially-correct flavor (chocolate) among four unrelated wrong flavors, which the judge scored 0 for not matching the reference at all.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Did not re-verify the other 4 stops; the clue_interval/total_intervals for this question point only to the single 176308-176857 window, so the 4 additional flavors are off-target regardless of their own individual accuracy.

rollouts.failure_point: Same misinterpretation as rollout 2; scored slightly higher (1 vs 0) likely because the chocolate/vanilla item was listed first and phrased closer to the reference, but four extra wrong flavors still diluted correctness enough to earn only 1.

rollouts.answer: He got a chocolate-and-vanilla swirl (twist)-i.e., chocolate mixed with vanilla-and ate it as he continued through Shanghai. The shop footage shows him ordering the chocolate-vanilla combination and receiving the cone.

decisive_steps.what_happened: Agent checked three candidate ice-cream moments via clip_qa but correctly judged only the 176298-176478 one belongs to the actual 'Five Snowman' stop and reported just that flavor pair (chocolate-vanilla) instead of enumerating all three as separate stores.

rollouts.failure_point: Same systematic flavor misread (chocolate-vanilla vs. reference taro-chocolate) as rollouts 0/1, but correct scoping to the single relevant store kept the answer concise and earned the same partial credit (2) as rollouts 0/1.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Consistent with rollouts 0/1's flavor reading of the same 176298-176478 window; no additional independent verification performed beyond reusing the frame check.

db_evidence.notes: The correct time window (176308-176857 logical / video 14 offset ~19030-19579) is easily retrievable by both semantic_search and run_sql across all 5 rollouts, and every rollout that stayed scoped to it converged on the same flavor description. However, no row in episodes, visual_clips, topic_facts, or event_steps anywhere in the DB contains the word 'taro' (verified with SQL LIKE '%taro%' returning 0 rows), and the visual sub-agent (clip_qa), which samples raw frames, also consistently reports 'chocolate and vanilla' / 'vanilla soft-serve' for this segment. Direct frame inspection (t=176440-176450, source video 14 offset ~19162-19172) shows a cream/off-white cone with a brown drizzle, which is visually consistent with what both the DB captions and clip_qa reported, not an obviously purple/lavender taro color under the shop's mixed white/green lighting - so the flavor mislabeling likely originates upstream in the offline captioning pipeline and is reinforced rather than corrected by clip_qa's own frame sampling.

root_causes: Systematic flavor misidentification upstream of the agent: the offline caption/description pipeline (episodes, visual_clips, topic_facts, event_steps) never records 'taro' for this segment and instead consistently describes the cone as chocolate-vanilla/vanilla; the clip_qa visual sub-agent, sampling the same or similar frames, reproduces the same wrong reading, so no amount of better retrieval by the main agent could recover the correct flavor from this evidence chain.

Question-phrase misinterpretation in 2 of 5 rollouts (2, 3): 'Five Snowman' (a store/brand name, as later confirmed by the single-store correct answer given by rollouts 0/1/4) was read as a literal instruction to find and enumerate five separate ice-cream stops across the whole video, producing four extra unrelated wrong flavors that diluted or eliminated the partial credit the single correct 'chocolate' token would otherwise have earned.

No DB text ever contains 'snowman', near the correct time window, so agents had no lexical anchor to confirm the store's actual brand/name and had to rely entirely on semantic_search and the (mistaken) visual reading.
what_worked: Rollouts 0, 1, and 4 correctly localized the single relevant Shanghai ice-cream-shop interval (176298-176478) via semantic_search/run_sql and correctly recognized it was one store rather than five, which is why they scored 2 (partial credit for 'chocolate') instead of 0-1.
clip_qa was invoked appropriately in all 5 rollouts to directly verify the flavor from frames rather than trusting captions alone, even though the frames themselves were misread.
transferable_lessons: When a question names something in a way that looks like a store/brand name (e.g. 'Five Snowman'), do not assume 'five' is a literal count to enumerate; first search for the name/brand directly (SQL LIKE on the exact phrase, semantic_search restricted to a narrow time window near any independently-found candidate) before broadening to a video-wide search for multiple occurrences.

If a caption-derived flavor/color read (e.g. 'vanilla') cannot be corroborated by any other independent database row (no brand name hit, no matching entity), treat clip_qa's answer as low-confidence rather than final, since clip_qa can inherit the same visual misjudgment as the offline captions when sampling similar frames under difficult lighting.

When enumerating multiple candidate moments across a long video for a question with only one true relevant window, don't submit all found candidates as if the question asked for a full inventory; scope the answer down to the clue interval indicated by other retrieval signals to avoid diluting partial credit.
open_questions: Whether the true flavor at the shop is genuinely taro (purple) and was simply invisible/ambiguous in the compressed/low-light stream frames sampled, or whether the reference answer 'Taro + Chocolate' was derived from a different visual cue (e.g., signage, translated Chinese text on the illuminated menu board) that no rollout's SQL or semantic search ever surfaced.
Whether 'Five Snowman' is meant to be a literal store-chain name (e.g. a Chinese ice-cream chain) that should have been searchable via OCR'd sign text not captured in the current caption pipeline.
